investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official homepage, its full events listing page, and two individual event detail pages. The events listing page is server-rendered with a fully structured static HTML event list (date spans, title, 'starting from' price, detail link) requiring no JSON-LD/API discovery. Each event detail page additionally links its own per-event 'Add to Calendar' ICS file, which was also fetched directly and retained.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official events listing page (https://www.uber-eats-music-hall.de/events/all) immediately exposed 71 distinct upcoming event entries as fully server-rendered static HTML: each event card/row carries a structured date (weekday/day/month/year/hour markup), a title heading, a 'starting from' ticket price, and a stable detail-page URL encoding the event slug and start datetime. Two sampled event detail pages confirmed the same fields plus a discoverable per-event ICS ('Add to Calendar') link exposing a UTC-normalized DTSTART. No JSON-LD, WordPress, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal was present, and none was needed — Level 1 fully answered the investigation question.

venue_reference: Verti Music Hall (now renamed Uber Eats Music Hall as of 22 March 2024 — the venue formerly called Verti Music Hall; large concert hall, Uber-Platz/Mercedes-Platz, Friedrichshain, Berlin)

identity.notes: The retained homepage's own <title> reads 'Uber Eats Music Hall | Uber Eats Music Hall' and the page repeatedly self-identifies as operated by AEG/Anschutz (e.g. an 'Anschutz hilft e.V.' partner link and an 'Uber Platz' venue-district link), at the venue's own domain uber-eats-music-hall.de. This is the venue's own current official web presence — the venue known to the public (and named in this investigation's brief) as 'Verti Music Hall' was renamed 'Uber Eats Music Hall' in March 2024 following a naming-rights change; verti-music-hall.de now redirects to/aliases the same operator. This is a genuine renamed-venue identity, not a different candidate.

site_classification.platform: Custom AEG Presents Europe venue CMS (image/asset host 'production.carbonhouse.com', shared markup/behaviour pattern also seen on the AEG-operated Uber Arena site) — server-rendered event listing and detail pages. No WordPress, JSON-LD, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal detected on any fetched page. Each event detail page links a per-event ICS ('Add to Calendar') file, generated server-side and readable without JS.

start_date.notes: Each event's own structured date markup states weekday, day, month, and year together in one place per event ('Freitag, 02. Okt. 2026'), and the per-event ICS DTSTART (20261002T180000Z, a full UTC instant) independently corroborates the same calendar date in Europe/Berlin local time. No cross-record combination needed.

time.notes: The HTML states a floating local time text ('20:00 Uhr', Europe/Berlin) directly on the same event card/detail page as the title. The per-event ICS DTSTART independently and directly states the same instant as a full UTC timestamp (20261002T180000Z = 20:00 CEST). Recorded value is the ICS's own explicit UTC instant, the more precise of the two directly-stated forms.

end.notes: The HTML never states an end time (only a start time and, separately, doors/'Einlass' time). The per-event ICS does carry a DTEND, but comparing two independently sampled events (Amelie Lens: DTSTART 18:00Z / DTEND 20:00Z; Beartooth: DTSTART 18:00Z / DTEND 20:00Z) shows DTEND is exactly DTSTART+2h in both cases — a fixed default duration the calendar generator appears to synthesize, not a genuine venue-stated end time. Not promoted to a proven fact per the policy's anti-guessing rule.

venue_location.notes: Individual event cards/detail pages do not restate the venue name or address per event — this is the venue's own single-venue official site (every /events/detail/ page is inherently this one venue), matching the same NOT_PRESENT-per-record treatment already used for razzmatazz-barcelona-01 (resolved via source_id, not a per-record field, since only one physical venue is in scope).

source_record_id.notes: Each event's own detail-page URL path (slug + start-datetime suffix, e.g. '/events/detail/amelie-lens/2026-10-02-2000') is the site's own canonical, directly-stated permalink for that specific occurrence — the same documented URL-slug stable-identifier strategy already used for moog-barcelona-01/LAV (ingestion/lav/discovery.mjs). The slug alone is NOT unique (e.g. 'freya-skye' appears twice, on 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20), so the full slug+datetime path is the smallest directly-stated unique key. A secondary numeric CMS id is also directly observable in each event's own ICS link path (e.g. '/events/ical/amelie-lens/4002/2'), corroborating that the platform maintains its own stable internal ids, though the slug+datetime permalink is used here as it is the field genuinely surfaced on every event record without a second fetch.

event_url.notes: Each event card's own detail-page link, stated directly.

price.notes: Each listing card shows only an 'ab' (starting-from) price string per event (e.g. 'ab 47,50 €') — a real, directly-stated value, but a lower-bound indicator rather than a complete price/tier breakdown, so not promoted to a single proven price value.
